results.title: ChatGPT Dots Alternatives: 5 best agents to use in 2026 (Free & Paid) | Saner.AI
results.content:
Autonomy: how much the tool does without being prompted. That's the core promise of Dots.
 Proactivity: whether it surfaces what matters on its own or waits for instructions.
 Setup friction: minutes to first useful result, and whether you need a terminal.
 Trust controls: approvals, activity logs and what happens to your credentials. An agent with your email login is only as good as its guardrails.
 Real cost for one person: the price you'll actually pay for daily use, including usage caps.
 Availability: region, platform, and plan restrictions. This is Dots' biggest weakness.

## What are the Best ChatGPT Dots alternatives?

the Best ChatGPT Dots alternatives are Grok Bot, Muse, OpenClaw, Claude Cowork and Saner.AI

## 1. Grok Bot: the closest thing to Dots, built by xAI [...] ## 1. Grok Bot: the closest thing to Dots, built by xAI

Grok Bot is xAI's always-on agent product. Instead of one assistant, you get a roster of named bots, each with a role, all sharing one dedicated cloud computer with a browser, file system and terminal. Structurally, it's the nearest match to Dots. It has one feature Dots doesn't: you can screen-record yourself doing a workflow once, and Grok Bot turns that recording into a repeatable skill

## 5. Claude Cowork: the Dots alternative for document-heavy work

Claude Cowork is Anthropic's agent mode inside the Claude apps. You describe an outcome, step away, and come back to finished work: formatted documents, organized files, synthesized research. Cowork runs sessions remotely in the cloud (in beta), so your work follows you across desktop, web, and mobile.

results.title: OpenDots VS ChatGPT : Who Wins?
results.content:
The script reviews OpenDots, an open-source alternative to ChatGPT’s new Dots AI agents, and compares their pros and cons. It shows how Dots works inside ChatGPT with agents like “Big J,” including the ability to talk via phone calls, but notes limited model flexibility and that it isn’t open source. OpenDots, from CopilotKit, can be set up from GitHub, supports different/local models, and can run an agent “computer” in the cloud via a Composio API, but is less personalized since it lacks ChatGPT history and may be harder for non-technical users; ChatGPT’s UI is also described as cleaner. The creator recommends OpenDots for technical users, Dots for non-technical users, prefers GroqBot in side-by-side testing, and mentions Hermes Bot Screen as another alternative, promoting training in [...] [6:38] profit boarding.
